title: Electrical Service Upgrade for a Two-Unit Home: From 200A to 400A with AFCI and Surge Protection
summary: This Old House documents a two-unit home undergoing an electrical service upgrade tied to a broader renovation that includes new HVAC, appliances, and updated siding. The episode centers on determining electrical load and upgrading from a 200-amp service to a 400-amp service, driven by increased demand from two units and new equipment. It explains the path of utility power (the overhead triplex and point of attachment), the upgrade to a larger meter can, and the shift to two meters and two service panels to serve each unit. Interior wiring updates are noted (BX to NM wiring) along with modern code protections, including arc-fault circuit interrupters and surge protection installed at the panels. The video combines architectural context with practical electrical upgrading steps, emphasizing who is responsible for overhead infrastructure and how new protections help safeguard the home’s circuits and appliances.
